text: Karankawa is an extinct language of the East Texas coast. Karankawa is generally considered a language isolate (a language unrelated to any other known language), though some linguists have tried to link it to the Coahuiltecan, Hokan, or even Carib language families.

title: The Karankawa Want You to Know They’re Not Extinct
text: August 20, 2024 - The powwows were important Native American bonding experiences, but the singing, dancing, and drumming tended to come from native societies in Mexico or on the northern plains whose traditions might have only a tenuous connection to those of the Karankawa. All that’s left of the Karankawa language are 450 or so words set down in journals by French captives or Spanish explorers or compiled in the late nineteenth century by a Swiss ethnologist named Albert Samuel Gatschet.
